questions.question: What does caching change in cost_per_query when the system prompt is a cache hit?
options: The user turn becomes free and the output is billed at the input price
Every token is charged at the cache-write premium on a hit
Only the system-prompt portion uses the cache-read fraction; the user turn and output remain full-price
Caching changes quality routing but never changes token cost
questions.explanation: The function applies CACHE_READ_FRACTION to cached system tokens. User tokens and output tokens are still billed with their normal input and output prices.

questions.question: Which tier does route choose for a high-confidence query in the COMPLEX_REASONING category?
options: HAIKU, because high confidence always selects the cheapest tier
SONNET, because complex queries bypass only the Haiku branch
HAIKU, if the combined token count is under 600
OPUS, because complex reasoning is routed to the frontier tier first
questions.explanation: The first branch in route checks category COMPLEX_REASONING and returns OPUS. Confidence and token count do not override that quality requirement.

questions.question: What tier handles a 250-input/120-output structured-extraction query with confidence=0.92?
options: HAIKU
SONNET
OPUS
No route, because the output is structured
questions.explanation: The total is 370 tokens, below MAX_TOKENS_FOR_HAIKU=600; confidence exceeds 0.85; and the category is STRUCTURED_EXTRACTION. The cheapest qualifying tier is HAIKU.

questions.question: What happens to a SHORT_QA query with confidence=0.55, even when its input is short?
options: It routes to HAIKU because the task is short
It routes to OPUS because confidence is below the Sonnet threshold of 0.70
It routes to SONNET because every SHORT_QA task uses the balanced tier
It is rejected without a model tier
questions.explanation: The low-confidence guard runs before the short-query branch. Since 0.55 is below MIN_CONFIDENCE_SONNET=0.70, route returns OPUS.

questions.question: At cache_hit_rate=1.0, which cost components remain full-price in cost_per_query?
options: Only the cache write
Only the system prompt
The user input and model output; the system prompt uses the cache-read rate
None, because a full cache hit makes the query free
questions.explanation: A complete hit changes only the system-prompt charge to 10% of input price. User-turn input and generated output are still charged normally.
